newsitem.title: USA: Pepsico's Taco Bell found liable in suit.
newsitem.headline: Pepsico's Taco Bell found liable in suit.

text.p: A Washington state jury Tuesday ruled against PepsiCo Inc.'s Taco Bell unit in a class-action suit filed on behalf 12,000 current and former employees.
The jury found the restaurant chain wilfully permitted a pattern of off-the-clock work at its 62 company-owned restaurants in the state from 1992 to the present.

In a 212-page verdict, the jury said Taco Bell managers in Washington state intentionally acted to deprive workers of wages by allowing them to work before and after their designated shifts without compensation.
The jury deliberated for eight days after a trial that lasted two months in King County Superior Court. Any damages would be determined in a second phase of the trial.
An attorney for the plaintiffs said 1,500 people currently work for Taco Bell restaurants in the state, but because of the chain's high turnover rate, there were 12,000 people in the affected class.
